items.title: 52043_Herman Autrey oral history interview
items.q: Charlie Turner is bass player... we had a bus. It took the small group, the six guys

ctx.x: Yeah, well I have a -- I've got to tell this. We went up to -- uh, not to far up into Connecticut. By golly, what's the name of the damn town? Anyway, we went up there, so when the bus -- we had a bus. It took the small group, the six guys -- (laughs) -- we stopped right in front of the joint. A lot of guys run out to see, oh here's the band.

And now -- I've got to name these guys. Charlie Turner is bass player. He weighed 290 pounds, at least, you know. And that's a pretty good sized man. At that time Fats was weighing 285, 90, maybe three, you know. At that time Herman Autrey was weighing about 245 or 50. Emmett Matthews was weighing about the same. And we had a drummer with us who is now -- he's working in the parks. He works for the Park Service. The thing here in New York? Uh -- uh, uh, uh, he's six foot three or four. items.q: And see Charlie knew what was happening, so Charlie said well cut me in too.

ctx.x: they want to get me out of the way. And I say Kirkaby, the bass player, Charlie Turner, yeah, who was a contractor. That's the word I was trying to --

Yeah, yeah. And see Charlie knew what was happening, so Charlie said well cut me in too. Which I don't blame him. You know. What the hell. I knew he was stealing, you look at him, just like a politician. Throw a few bucks my way, and go ahead. What the hell.
